name: Keoni Snipes
strengths: Snipes uses a 6-5 EDGE frame and length to engage blockers early and disrupt the pocket before OL can reset.
Snipes chases with a high motor — tracks perimeter runs sideline-to-sideline and still finishes with closing burst.
Snipes shows stand-up / hand-in-dirt flexibility — comfortable rushing or working in space for a multiple front.
weaknesses: Snipes needs a fuller hand-counter package beyond first-step athleticism when tackles latch.
Snipes still has to add functional strength and keep pad level to set the edge vs power and avoid wash-down blocks.
comparison: Snipes comps to Myles Murphy — listed 6-5 / 245 vs Murphy’s ~6-5 / 275 EDGE mold (same height, long-limb rusher frame); then matching length, motor, and developmental pass-rush tools (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Snipes projects to develop into Florida’s EDGE room with Year-1 special-teams / sub-package rush snaps, Year-2 compete for a rotational every-down role, and Year-3+ starter upside if the length + motor add mass and a counter package.
schemeFit: Snipes fits a hybrid 3-4 / 4-3 that wants a long JACK/EDGE who can rush, chase, and work gap-exchange without losing effort on backside plays.
staffNotes: FILM VERIFIED 2026-08-09 from Saraland sophomore highlights (Keoni Snipes #11, ~5:03). Watched full package — length, motor, versatility; hands + anchor polish.
recruitingStory: Keoni Snipes is a 4-star EDGE listed 6-5 / 245 from Saraland (AL) — SEC-offer EDGE with Florida in the live chase mix.
angle: Long Alabama EDGE with chase traits — Florida can develop the counters into starter upside.
insiderNotes: Watched Saraland sophomore tape. Snipes wins with length and effort; next step is hands and setting the edge.
